artDirection: HYBRID + AUTHORED VECTOR. Image generation is BLOCKED on this workspace (403 insufficient_permissions: image_video_generation), so all new art is hand-authored SVG rasterised to PNG — which is actually superior for flat vector: exact hex, zero gradient, precise outline weights, no derivative-work risk. Plants: flatten-pipeline experiment in progress. Original art only; Toca is the bar, never a source.

pieces.name: Toca standard + critic rubric
pieces.note: Rubric grounded in measured pixels from real Toca frames: pure #000000 outlines at ~1.4% of object height, absolutely flat fills (zero gradient/grain), pure white only 1% of pixels, 3-4 hue families, flat two-tone shading at dV 0.08-0.18. 10 scored categories; any category <=6 fails outright.

pieces.name: Three.js foundation (stage/tween/particles/textures/input)
pieces.note: Verified by screenshot: sprites on correct layers, DPR 1.75, 6/6 textures, live tweens, pooled particles, reduced-motion path, 44px hit enforcement, context-loss overlay. Agent found+fixed idle-loop suppression and degenerate-world bugs during its own verification.

log.msg: Critic RETRACTED four of its own suspicions after checking source, and flagged them so we would not fix what is not broken. That is the behaviour I want.
New findings: prop_seed silhouette merges with its mound (0px gap where 8px required), worm segment ticks render at 0.4px, and all 3 cloud variants share one recipe including the identical drip lobe.
Sharpest structural note: the dirt plot mixes projections — side-on rim with a top-down hole — which is WHY it reads as food rather than ground.
Round 4 building.
Motion fixes COMPLETE and committed. Motion fraction 0.35 -> 0.96; settle 383 -> 300ms; every tap now answers.
Builder used git stash to re-measure the ORIGINAL under identical conditions rather than trusting remembered numbers.

Two real bugs found: spawnCritter bailed on document.hidden (so any player returning from another tab had an empty sky forever), and paintDayNight overwrote plant colour every frame, erasing the reduced-motion acknowledgement.
I independently verified: all JS passes node --check, confetti fully gone from CSS+HTML, zero bare linear easing.
Re-critic spawned with an explicit brief to hunt for OVER-correction — 96% of sprites moving could read as jittery rather than alive.
Session rate limit killed 3 agents mid-flight. Assessed what survived on disk before respawning anything.
Kit expansion had nearly finished: all 3 stress-test plants + new primitives + automated gates were already written.
Ran the gates myself: G1 diversity PASS (worst pair 0.647, was 0.930) and G2 per-plant saturation PASS. Committed.
Confirmed visually that the kit now builds MECHANICAL plants — robot rosebush with panels and bolts, xylophone of graduated bars. It is no longer a foliage kit.
Dirt plot round 4 died mid-fix and now reads as a mountain range. My redirection: stop redesigning the silhouette, put the identity in surface TEXTURE.
Reduced concurrency to 2 Opus agents — the rate limit was self-inflicted.
FAN-OUT GATE round 2: FAIL — but narrow, mechanical, documentation-only. No art needs redrawing.
Kit code CONFIRMED scale-ready: the critic authored 3 of the hardest remaining plants (escalator, narwhal nettle, airplane tree) from kit calls alone with no missing primitive.
Blind A/B reached a genuine TIE at the reference standard — first time.
Killer finding: ten agents read KIT.md, not _kit.py. The doc still publishes the FAILED OL_FINE=7 and documents none of the new branch/rectilinear primitives.

Silent trap proven: docs say trunk_chunky(...lean) but the code 6th positional is root_seed, so two plants both written lean=0 emit byte-identical feet — the shared-foot failure, reintroduced invisibly.

Verifier holes found by adversarial testing: _verify.py <one-id> prints G1 PASS after zero comparisons and exits 0 — the exact command a fan-out author runs. IDS is a hardcoded 9-name list, so plants 10-78 are never enrolled.
Primer fix underway on Sonnet (mechanical, precisely specified); I will verify the doc-vs-code claims myself with greps before any fan-out.
Dirt plot PASSED at round 5. The strategic inversion worked: calm silhouette, identity in surface texture.
Key device: shed clods on the grass — a mass that sheds crumbs is the one thing a loaf, rock or molar never does.
MAJOR GAP FOUND: none of the flat art was wired in. grep -rn art/flat js/ returned nothing — 25 world assets + 9 plants sitting unused while the game rendered the old claymation.
Wiring agent building an ALIAS MAP rather than scattered path edits, so the remaining 69 plants light up one line at a time.
It must also retune sizing: the flat plot is a wide 2.4:1 bed where the old art was a tall dome, and the plot had become the shortest object on screen despite being the primary tap target.
Primer FIXED and verified: KIT.md now matches code, signatures corrected, _kit.png re-laid out, verifier holes closed.
Durable guard added: _check_palette.py reads _kit.py live and fails on ANY hex drift — the second automated gate protecting future agents.
It caught a conflict I introduced: my dirt-plot commit recoloured soil in the brief without updating the kit.
Resolved by separating BARK from ground SOIL — different materials. Trunks must stay cooler or they compete with the plot for the focal weight we deliberately gave it.
Result: 31/31 tokens match, both gates pass (36 comparisons), and zero plant PNGs changed — the rename was purely nominal.
Flat art WIRED and committed — the world now reads as one coherent flat-vector scene.
Verified by my own screenshot: flat beds with real variants, grass tufts, hill bands, faced sun, and the flat butterfly bush / sunflower / apple tree.
Visible clash confirmed exactly as the builder honestly reported: the glossy caterpillar vine sits between two flat plants, and claymation critters fly over a flat world.
FAN-OUT BEGUN: 69 plants remain. Waves A-G and H-O building concurrently into separate build modules; P-Z queued to keep concurrency at 2.
Two follow-ups logged: DOM modal previews bypass the texture loader (choice cards still show claymation portraits), and the sun sits behind the cloud layers so its new face gets covered.
Wave A-G COMPLETE: 18 plants, gates PASS at 1225 comparisons, zero palette drift.
Verified at game size myself — these have real charm. Burger Bush, Donut Tree, Duck Bloom and Giraffe Grass all land instantly at 128px.
Builder self-assessment was well calibrated: it named the fern as weakest and the ant workers as collapsing, and both were exactly what I saw.
Wave P-Z spawned (28 plants) with an explicit warning about the 0.690 spruce/UFO near-collision, since several of its plants are conical.
27 of 78 plants now authored.
Wave H-O COMPLETE: 23 plants, gates PASS at 1334 comparisons, zero drift. 50 of 78 now authored.
Verified at game size myself — hotdog hedge, owl orchid, octopus oakleaf and ketchup cactus are genuinely funny at 128px.
Second builder in a row whose self-assessment matched my own eyes exactly (hibiscus generic, kale generic, marshmallow trunk bare).

Kit defect found and correctly NOT fixed: hidden sleepy brows render under the 11px floor because _brow_marks hardcodes width while face() scales the rig. It respected the shared-file boundary and reported instead.
Watch item: worst pair in the set is now 0.699 (norway-spruce / quail-quillplant) — razor-thin against the 0.70 gate. quail is a P-Z plant, so that wave owns resolving it.
ALL 78 PLANTS AUTHORED AND LIVE. Full-set gates pass: 3003 comparisons, worst pair 0.693, zero drift.
Wired all 78 myself by generating overrides + measured metrics; content boxes for the original 9 came out identical to the hand-tuned ones, so sizing was not degraded.
Verified in-game with a 12-plant garden: the world reads as one coherent flat-vector game.
NEW ISSUE I found: with a full garden, plants overlap heavily across rows (plantH is allowed 1.75x rowH). Readable but cluttered — routing to the coherence critic rather than guessing.
Remaining claymation outliers: critters, stage-1 sprout, lock signs, rain clouds, moon/stars/rainbow.
FINISHING RUN. Inventory: 18 assets still claymation (7 critters, 5 sky, 2 garden, 4 fx).

Found a bigger gap than the art: DOM modal previews build raw tags and never touch the texture loader, so the letter picker, sticker book and celebration card ALL still show claymation portraits over a flat world.
Two agents running: remaining flat art, and the code gaps (DOM previews, sun behind clouds, unused sun expressions, deferred kit brow fix + full plant rebuild).
ALL scene textures are now flat vector — 122 overrides, zero claymation left in the WebGL world.
DOM previews fixed via a bridge module, deliberately NOT published from main3d.js: that module bails without WebGL, and on a locked-down Chromebook the modals ARE the game.
Kit brow defect fixed: 22 plants had brows under the 11px floor. Rebuild left 30 faced plants byte-identical — incidental proof the rasteriser is deterministic.
I found a gap no inventory had caught: the HUD icons and logo are DOM images, so they never appeared in scene-texture checks. Now being authored flat — the last claymation surface.
COHERENCE PASS RUNNING: first agent to play the whole game end to end, and to settle whether a full 12-plant garden reads as lush or cluttered.
